scenes.heading: Factorising quadratic trinomials
scenes.sub: Find two numbers: multiply, then add
scenes.say: How do you turn x squared plus seven x plus twelve back into two brackets? In this video you will learn the multiply-and-add method.
scenes.caption: How do you turn x² + 7x + 12 back into two brackets? In this video you will learn the multiply-and-add method.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Two ages multiply to 12 and add to 7: they must be 3 and 4
scenes.breaks: Ages are positive, but your two numbers can be negative, so watch the signs.
scenes.say: Think like a detective. Two ages multiply to twelve and add to seven. The only pair that fits is three and four. Factorising works the same way: find two numbers that multiply to the last term and add to the middle coefficient.

scenes.heading: The pattern
scenes.say: Here is why it works. Expanding x plus p, times x plus q, gives x squared plus p plus q times x, plus p q. So the two numbers multiply to c and add to b.

scenes.heading: The area model
scenes.say: First the rectangle, then its sides, x plus three and x plus four, then the parts inside. The corner box is three times four, twelve. The two strips, three x and four x, add to seven x.
scenes.caption: First the rectangle, then its sides, x + 3 and x + 4, then the parts. The corner is 3 × 4 = 12. The strips 3x and 4x add to 7x.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Factorise x² − 2x − 15.
scenes.say: Factorise x squared minus two x minus fifteen. We need two numbers that multiply to negative fifteen and add to negative two. The product is negative, so the signs differ. Three and negative five work. The answer is x plus three, times x minus five.
scenes.caption: Factorise x² − 2x − 15. We need two numbers that multiply to −15 and add to −2. The product is negative, so the signs differ. 3 and −5 work: (x + 3)(x − 5).

scenes.heading: Common factor first
scenes.question: Factorise fully 3x² − 21x + 30.
scenes.say: Always look for a common factor first. Three x squared minus twenty-one x plus thirty has a common factor of three. Inside, we need two numbers that multiply to ten and add to negative seven: negative two and negative five. Keep the three at the front.
scenes.caption: Always look for a common factor first. 3x² − 21x + 30 = 3(x² − 7x + 10). Two numbers that multiply to 10 and add to −7: −2 and −5. Keep the 3 at the front: 3(x − 2)(x − 5).

points: Find numbers: multiply to c, add to b
scenes.say: Quick recap. Take out any common factor first. Then find two numbers that multiply to the constant and add to the x coefficient. Use the signs as clues, and always expand to check. Now try the practice questions!
